# QUESTIONs with `tags` `social-ontology`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Social ontology** — what social facts, groups, institutions and social kinds are, and what makes them exist — collective intentionality, joint commitment, status functions, convention, social construction, and whether groups can be agents or minds (group: philosophy; ADR-017).

| [QUESTION-049](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-049.md) | When a corporation is said to know or intend something no member does, is the attribution tracking a mind the corporation has, or shaping the corporation to meet it? | An unmarked tension between two THEORYs the record holds, raised by the synthesis review of 2026-10-11. | [QUESTION-053](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-053.md) | Does organizational affect need a group subject, a state of the group not reducible to its members' states, or only the synchronized convergence of members' affect? | An unmarked tension between two THEORYs the record holds, raised by the synthesis review of 2026-10-11. [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) (Huebner) allows a group to be in an emotional state that is not its members' states in aggregation. [THEORY-126](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-126.md) (von Scheve and Ismer) makes collective emotion synchronous convergence with no group subject. | [QUESTION-070](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-070.md) v4 | When an organized whole manipulates, as a learning system exploiting documented biases or a network of state channels does, is it the same wrong when no member intends to manipulate, and whose agency does the wrong run through? | Most definitions of manipulation now filed build in a manipulator's intent, though Noggle's survey treats that requirement as contested and asks this question's first part of a selecting algorithm. | [QUESTION-073](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) | Are teasing and reproach individuated by the speaker's communicative intention, or partly by a frame the parties sustain together and by their standing? | Raised by [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) and [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) on 2026-10-10. Intention-based accounts of illocution (Grice; Strawson 1964; Bach and Harnish 1979) plausibly individuate teasing by the speaker's intention. Goffman's account of keying a play frame and Austin's securing of uptake ([LIT-785](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-785.md), unread) are the tradition's replies. None of these is read here. An answer would read them and find a case in which the speaker's intention is held fixed and the act verdicts of informed participants change with the parties' standing or uptake. | Open |
| [QUESTION-082](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-082.md) | When a polity is steered by polling, whose reasons do its decisions carry: its members', its own, or none? | Raised by the owner on 2026-10-13, in conversation, as an implication of [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) for "how modern politics leans so heavily on polling data", and sharpened by the owner from a whole's good to a whole's reasons. | [QUESTION-094](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-094.md) | When an organization allocates authority over related propositions to different processes by endorsement, what keeps its collective judgments consistent, and must that be a separate integration step as in judgment aggregation? | A4's List and Pettit connection, which it put as "Authority aggregation ≠ judgment aggregation ≠ collective rationality". | [QUESTION-118](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-118.md) | When a collective reproduces its organization through the replacement of all its members, what must stay causally continuous for the later organization to be the earlier one persisting, and not a similar one produced anew, and how is the question settled when several later collectives each continue it in a different respect? | A5 §7 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, with the branching part from A2 and A4. | [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md) | When a diffusely organized population with no procedure for collective judgment is credited with a stance, or with an effect on an outside institution, when is the credit due to the population as organized, and when is it a biased sample of what some members said or did? | A5 §3 and A7 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on a fanbase that "hates" its owner and on the Juggernaut line. [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) and [CLAIM-271](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-271.md) say a collective's intention or reasons can differ from its members'; both assume an organization that forms them.
